title: The day of Arafah
hookLine: the pilgrims stand on the plain, and others fast the day

cards: The month of the pilgrimage, the ninth day. A wide, bare plain outside Mecca, a low hill in the middle, the sun climbing. A crowd of pilgrims reaching past the edge of sight, most dressed alike in plain white.
Nobody is shopping. Nobody is sightseeing. From noon until sunset, they mostly just stand there, and ask.
And far away, in kitchens and offices, other Muslims skip breakfast that morning, because they're fasting the same day.

teach.h: THE NINTH DAY, AND THE PLAIN.
teach.b: Arafah is the ninth day of Dhu al-Hijjah, the month of the pilgrimage, and also the name of the plain itself. The Hajj has many rites: circling the Kaaba, walking between two hills, throwing pebbles, the sacrifice.
But the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ summed it up in two words, reported by Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud: the Hajj is Arafah. Miss the standing on that plain, and in the view of the scholars, you've missed the Hajj.
The standing is called wuquf. There's no fixed script for it. People pray, recite, weep, ask for forgiveness, ask for their families, in Arabic and in every other language.
Tirmidhi reports that the best supplication is the supplication of the day of Arafah. Sahih Muslim adds that there's no day on which Allah frees more people from the Fire. It's a day of history too.

teach.h: A FAREWELL, AND A FINISHED VERSE.
teach.b: Jabir's long account in Sahih Muslim has the Prophet giving his sermon at Arafah, on his farewell pilgrimage.
And Bukhari reports that one line of the Qur'an came down on a Friday at Arafah: This day have I perfected your religion for you. Now the other half of the picture.
For those at home, the tradition offers the fast. Sahih Muslim reports that fasting the day of Arafah is hoped to wipe away the sins of the year before and the year after.
The pilgrims usually don't fast; they need their strength to stand. Many others do.

teach.h: ONE DAY, TWO WAYS TO KEEP IT.
teach.b: One day, two ways of keeping it: standing on the plain, or fasting at your desk.

how: On the ninth of Dhu al-Hijjah, pilgrims stand on the plain of Arafah from midday to sunset in prayer and supplication, while many Muslims who are not on Hajj fast that day.

games.q: you can't go on Hajj this year. the day of Arafah arrives. what does the tradition offer you?
o: travel to the nearest hill and stand
games.why: fasting the day of Arafah is hoped to wipe away the sins of the year before and the year after (Muslim). one day, kept two ways.

practice: Sit or stand, whichever feels more like the plain, and choose one thing to give your full attention to, and only one: a person, a piece of work, a question you keep avoiding.
If you pray, ask for help with it, in any words you have; if not, simply stay with it and let everything else wait.
